chinese_source: Yijing, Nanhai Jigui Neifa Zhuan (Record of Buddhist Practices, sent home 691) and his Memoir of eminent monks
event: Yijing resides ten years at Nalanda and reports, as an administrator of monastic routine: more than 3,000 resident monks (Memoir: 3,500), eight halls, more than 300 apartments, and landed endowment of more than 200 villages accumulated from successive kings
date_raw: Tang, Xianheng to Chuigong eras; residence 673-685, Record sent home Tianshou 2 (691)
firmness_reason: Eyewitness with an administrative (not panegyric) register; his 300 apartments match the excavated ground-floor cell estimate (~250-320) and his 15 monks-per-village ratio is internally consistent with the Devapala plate's endowment rate — the dataset's anchor population witness
notes: Some manuscripts of the Record read 5,000 for the resident count; Takakusu judged 3,000 the correct reading. Even 3,000 exceeds the excavated core's design capacity (~450-650 cells), so his figure implies the unexcavated remainder of the walled complex and/or shared occupancy — see the capacity test.
references: Takakusu, A Record of the Buddhist Religion as Practised in India and the Malay Archipelago (1896)
Yijing, Nanhai Jigui Neifa Zhuan, T.2125
